label: late original-phase steps and <DEL>, gated by first token (p/a/m/r/d/k...)
explanation: Fires only during the original phase and on the <DEL> step, never in the copy phase (0 activations at t>L) and never at t<3. Rate rises with position: about 8% at orig_idx 4, 50% at 6, 79% at 8, and 44% at <DEL>; longer sequences carry most of the mass. Whether it fires depends strongly on the FIRST original token. With first token p or a, precision at t>=5 is about 0.9; with m/r/d/k/b/o/f/i it is about 0.7-0.8; with e/x/g/n/q/u/y it is under 0.2. So it reads as a late-in-the-prompt / end-of-input feature that carries a memory of the sequence onset. Later tokens also shift it in a graded, additive-looking way: high when the current input is n/e, or the previous 1-2 inputs are p/f/s/d, or a/p appear early. That is why a single first-token set captures about 82% of activation mass but with only about 0.7 precision and recall. Top activations (about 4.8) occur at t=7-9 in sequences that start with p or a, often on n/e inputs just before <DEL>. Activations at t=4 and on repeated tokens (in_first=0) are weaker and are mostly missed.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: p, a, r, d, m, k; least: n, g, x, e) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: n, e, x, v; delimiter step: <DEL>; copy phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=6, t=8.
